intro: Chang'e 3 landed in Mare Imbrium on December 14, 2013 — China's first soft landing on the Moon and the first lunar landing of any kind in 37 years (since Luna 24). Deployed the Yutu rover, which drove ~114 m before a control failure froze it in place for the remaining ~30 lunar days of survival. Confirmed China as the third nation with surface assets on the Moon.

images.caption: A full-size mockup of the Yutu rover — 140 kg, six wheels, with a ground-penetrating radar under the chassis.
A Long March 3B lifting off at night — the rocket that launched Chang'e 3 from Xichang on 1 December 2013.

A boulder on Mare Imbrium seen up close by Yutu, with the rover’s orbital-image inset of where it stood.
